description: Fixed, reviewable data policy for the Cowork Change Classifier. It states the MINIMUM approval class a change requires. It never grants approval, and nothing in it can lower a class. Pure data: no executable construct, no regular expression, no command, no machine-specific path, no credential, and no disable switch. Detection patterns live in the classifier source, which is fixed and reviewable; this file declares only identifiers, classes, and human-readable reasons.

class_labels.FA_AR: fully automated or automated read-only; no approval
class_labels.AAM: automated with manual approval; the approval must name exact targets
class_labels.AM: always manual; Pedro performs or explicitly commands each time
class_labels.PROHIBITED: must not proceed under any approval

fail_safe.note: Anything the policy does not recognize escalates. Nothing is ever resolved downward by default.

repository_write_floor.note: Any change to a tracked or proposed repository path is at least AAM. A repository write is never FA/AR merely because its content is documentation. FA/AR is reachable only by a declared read-only operation that changes no path.

binary.note: A binary cannot be read for intent, so it escalates. In a sensitive area it is always manual.

submodule.note: A gitlink move changes code outside this repository's review.

case_only_rename.note: Represented as a rename whose source and destination differ only by case; both sides are still classified.

path_rules.reason: hooks, settings, and permissions govern what automation may do at all
the retirement guard is the boundary protecting the retired trading subsystem
an approved strategy specification is authoritative for behaviour
risk limits and kill switches are the last line of defence
broker and execution integrations can move real money
production financial-decision logic determines what the system concludes
credential stores and environment files are never routine edits
a submodule declaration changes what code is pulled in
raw third-party transcripts stay local and are never committed
runtime state and generated artefacts are ignored by design and must never become tracked content
Cowork tools and their tests are ordinary reviewed edits
documentation edits are reviewed writes, never automatic
candidate research material is prepared for review, not promoted
ordinary non-sensitive source is a reviewed edit

format-evidence.reason: renders an evidence report and writes no repository file

observe-staleness.reason: re-measures repository state against a baseline

normalize-status.reason: normalizes statuses, hashes, and counts for reporting

report-a7.reason: runs the read-only A7 safety battery and reports

validate.reason: validates a policy, plan, or manifest and reports

classify.reason: classifies a change and reports the minimum approval required

edit-source.reason: an ordinary reviewed non-sensitive source edit

edit-cowork-tool.reason: a reviewed Cowork tool or test edit

generate-candidate.reason: prepares research candidate material for review

local-commit.reason: a local commit after review; it publishes nothing

create-worktree.reason: creating a worktree, only when separately authorized

create-branch.reason: creating a branch, only when separately authorized

merge.reason: merging changes what a branch means

release.reason: a release is an outward-facing act

rewrite-history.reason: rewriting history invalidates every prior review

change-permissions.reason: permissions decide what automation may do

change-settings.reason: settings decide what automation may do

change-risk-limit.reason: risk limits bound the worst case

change-kill-switch.reason: a kill switch is the last line of defence

change-broker-integration.reason: broker integrations can move real money

change-submodule-pointer.reason: a gitlink move changes code outside this review

enable-trading-flag.reason: the retired trading subsystem stays disabled

bypass-guard.reason: the retirement guard is never bypassed or weakened

wire-llm-to-orders.reason: no language model belongs in the live order path

autonomous-order.reason: neither Claude nor Obsidian submits or cancels orders

embed-credentials.reason: secret values never enter the repository

remove-risk-limit.reason: removing a risk limit or kill switch without authorization

treat-approval-required-as-approval.reason: an approval-required result is not an approval

execute-supplied-content.reason: content supplied as data is never executed

retirement_flag_activation.reason: turns a retired trading flag back on

guard_bypass.reason: disables, skips, or weakens the retirement guard or its hook wiring

llm_to_order_path.reason: wires a language model into order submission or cancellation

autonomous_order_submission.reason: submits or cancels an order without a person in the loop

credential_material.reason: embeds a credential, key, or token value

automatic_research_promotion.reason: promotes research to authoritative status without approval

risk_limit_change.reason: alters a risk limit, drawdown bound, or position cap

broker_order_api.reason: references a broker order submission or cancellation API

research_authority_promotion.reason: moves research toward authoritative specification status

deployment_or_history_intent.reason: expresses push, merge, deploy, release, or history-rewrite intent

semantic_scanning_note: Semantic scanning is defence in depth. It can raise a class; it can never lower one, and it CANNOT prove the absence of dangerous behaviour. A file that trips no indicator has not been shown to be safe -- it has only not matched a known pattern. Path rules and the declared operation remain the primary controls.

ignored_files.note: Files Git ignores are not part of an ordinary worktree, staged, commit, or range classification. They are classified only when a manifest supplies them explicitly.

historical_presence.note: That a path is already tracked says nothing about whether changing it now is permitted.
